newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent flat, rangebound, eyes on Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent flat, rangebound, eyes on Nigeria.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were little changed on Monday in thin, rangebound trade and dealers said they thought Nigeria was the most likely area to provide market direction.
June Brent was unchanged at $18.27 a barrel at 0937 GMT while May gas oil stood just 25 cents a tonne weaker at $165.25.

"It is pretty uninteresting, we have come in even quieter than expected," one IPE dealer said. "It is a rangebound scenario between $18.18 and $18.55 and we need to break one of those numbers for anything to happen."
"Maybe something new will come out of Nigeria," he added.
GNI research said a descending chart trendline dating from early January on the continuous chart was providing resistance at $18.51. Support would be found at $18, their daily report said.

A Shell official in Lagos said on Monday his company's Nigerian Forcados output remains 95,000 barrels per day (bpd) below normal because of continued ethnic clashes. Production could stay down for some time, he added.
Shell said on Friday it had declared force majeure on 20 percent of the 475,000 bpd Forcados blend output causing delays of two to three days from April 29 to May 30.
No cargo cancellations have yet been announced.
"That (Nigeria) is the main bullish influence to think about today," GNI said.
